## BLUF

Done. Hint labels now render in **JetBrains Mono NL** (the no-ligatures cut; letterforms
identical to JetBrains Mono), bundled into the assembly via pack URI and served from the
embedded copy, with a new hot-reload `HintFontFamily` key (default `JetBrains Mono NL`).
Replaces a hardcoded `Helvetica, Arial`. CI green; drop shipped. Plan:
[`20260813-213400_label-font-jetbrains-mono.plan.qmd`](20260813-213400_label-font-jetbrains-mono.plan.qmd).

## Why JetBrains Mono NL (not a Nerd Font)

Labels are typeable ASCII (A–Z + optional punctuation). A Nerd Font's icons live in the PUA
and cannot be typed as labels, and the A–Z letters render identically to the base font — so a
Nerd Font would add ~10–15 MB for zero label benefit. Plain JetBrains Mono gives the same look
at ~420 KB. The **NL cut** additionally disables programming ligatures, so a punctuation label
pair (e.g. `//`) renders literally rather than as a ligature. (Verified reasoning; the size
delta is measured from the staged TTFs: ~209 KB Regular + ~211 KB Bold + ~4 KB OFL.)

## What shipped (commit on `master`)

1. `be316f9 feat(overlay): bundle JetBrains Mono NL as the configurable label font`

**Files:** new `Fonts/JetBrainsMonoNL-Regular.ttf`, `Fonts/JetBrainsMonoNL-Bold.ttf`,
`Fonts/OFL.txt` (SIL OFL 1.1); edited `Views/HintCanvas.cs` (static `LabelTypeface` → instance
`_typeface` + `ResolveFontFamily`), `ViewModels/HintViewModel.cs` (`FontFamilyReadValue`),
`ViewModels/OverlayViewModel.cs` (`_fontFamilyRaw` + `EffectiveFontFamily`, both ctors),
`Services/OverlayActionConfig.cs` (`ReadHintFontFamily`), `App.config` (`HintFontFamily`),
`HuntAndPeck.csproj` (`<Resource>` ×2 + `<None>` OFL), `CLAUDE.md`. No new `.cs` files
(added methods/properties inline), so no new `<Compile>` includes needed.

## Decisions (from the design conversation)

- **Bundle plain JetBrains Mono** (not a Nerd Font) — chosen via the design fork: the labels
  are letters, so Nerd Font icons add weight with no visual benefit.
- **NL (no-ligatures) cut** — same letterforms, no punctuation-label ligature surprises.
- **Labels only** (`HintCanvas`); the chrome badges (`OverlayView.xaml`, still `Helvetica,
  Arial` / `Consolas`) are out of scope, deliberately.
- **App.config-only** (not added to Options) — consistent with Nudge*/Zone*/LeaderBindings,
  which are also hot-reload-via-config-only. Hot-reload still works (edit `hap.exe.config`,
  re-trigger).
- **Self-contained** — the bundled family name resolves to the embedded copy via pack URI, so
  the font renders even when not installed on the box.

## Verification

- **CI** (`.github/workflows/build.yml`, `windows-latest`, MSBuild + vstest) — **GREEN**
  (run `31706138066`, sha `be316f9`; Build + Test + Upload ✓ in 51s; only annotation is the
  pre-existing Node.js 20 deprecation, unrelated).
- **Font embedment** (verified, not assumed): `strings -e l` on the shipped `hap.exe` finds
  the full TTF name tables for BOTH `JetBrainsMonoNL-Regular` and `JetBrainsMonoNL-Bold`
  (Copyright, "JetBrains Mono NL Bold/Regular", "Version 2.304", OFL license string), plus the
  `./#JetBrains Mono NL` pack-URI reference from the code. The family name was parsed from the
  TTFs with `fc-query` + `fontTools` (both agree: nameID 1 = `JetBrains Mono NL`, no nameID 16)
  BEFORE writing the pack URI — load-bearing, because WPF silently falls back on a mismatch.
- **Manual (Windows box):** drop shipped to `$HAP_WIN_TEST_DIR/hap-font/hap.exe`; awaiting
  on-box visual check (CI cannot confirm the font renders — a wrong pack URI compiles yet
  falls back at runtime). To confirm: labels render monospace (vs proportional Helvetica); set
  `HintFontFamily=Consolas` and re-trigger → labels switch (installed-font path); unset →
  bundled default. **Quit the old `hap.exe` (tray → Exit) before launching.**

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Runtime pack-URI resolution** — the one untestable-on-Linux risk; every prerequisite is
  verified (font embedded, family name exact). On-box visual check is the final gate.
- **Chrome fonts** — badges/popup still use `Helvetica, Arial` / `Consolas`; a follow-up could
  bind them to the same family for a unified look (not requested).
- **Options dialog** — `HintFontFamily` is config-only (consistent with other advanced keys).
